apps.name: iBestSpeech
apps.subtitle: Keynote Gold voices as system voices.
apps.localizedDescription:
Keynote Gold voices as system voices on iPhone and iPad, working with VoiceOver, Spoken Content and anything using the system voices, all on the device and offline. Bring your own Keynote Gold engine file: the app imports it at run time.

This build includes voice data that is not part of the open code and belongs to its owners. It is included for personal accessibility use, is not covered by the code licence, and will be removed if a rights holder asks.

versions.localizedDescription:
# iBestSpeech 1.0.14

Four pronunciation fixes, all measured against the built engine first.

**LLM and LLMs name every letter.** The rules collapse the doubled L
("llama" needs that; initials don't), so "LLMs" read "ell-em-ess". Spaced
letters follow the file's own convention (MIDI, HDMI).

**Y'all stays one syllable.** The apostrophe split it into "yuh-all";
plain "yawl" is byte-identical to "yall" on every English build, which is
the wanted sound. Both casings.

**Full-width punctuation folds to ASCII.** A full-width question mark made
the 1995 build return no audio at all for the whole phrase — which is how
a notification lost everything after its Chinese run. U+FF01–U+FF5E now
fold in the same pass as the other typographic forms.

**Ubuntu is "oo boon too" again.** The source had drifted to "too boon
too" while the shipped build still carried the right reading; regenerating
restores it with no behavior change.

Verified by the SSML suite (170 checks) and the engine word-path probes
behind each entry.

# iBestSpeech 1.0.13

Fourteen commits since 1.0.12, and two of them are worth the update on their
own.

**The app now has an icon.** 1.0.12 shipped without one — the archive had no
`Assets.car` and `Info.plist` never declared `CFBundleIconName`, which is what
App Store Connect rejects with ITMS-90022. It installs with a proper icon now.

**The preview no longer stops dead.** The ellipsis fix already ran in the
VoiceOver extension, but the app's own preview handed the engine the text as
typed — so the same notification spoke correctly in VoiceOver and stopped in
the preview, which is the path you test with. The preview now runs the same
text layer.

**You can load a whole NVDA addon.** Instead of finding the right DLL inside
an addon by hand, pick the `.nvda-addon` itself and the voices come out of it.
An addon is an ordinary zip, and the archives disagree about where a DLL
lives — depth 1 to 6, some Windows-built with backslashes where the spec wants
slashes, one keeping its engine outside `synthDrivers/`, four of the twelve on
this machine containing no DLL at all, and the largest one belonging to a PDF
library. So nothing is decided by name, path or size: every candidate is handed
to the engine and kept only if it actually speaks. Verified against the real
archives — the BestSpeech addon yields all thirteen of its voices, and the four
without a Keynote Gold engine yield nothing, with no false positives.

**The About screen shows the real version and build**, and the all-caps section
headers are gone — the engine spells an all-caps run letter by letter, so
"Your voice files" was being read out as a string of capitals by the app's own
voices.

Also in this release: the signed App Store build and TestFlight upload path,
and the extension's version can no longer drift from the app's, which is an
upload failure waiting to happen.

The public build still carries no voice data. The tables belong to the people
who made them; you import your own Keynote Gold file, and the files you load
stay on your device.

apps.name: iTruVoice
apps.subtitle: TruVoice voices as system voices.
apps.localizedDescription:
TruVoice voices (Peter, Julia, Sidney and the rest) as system voices on iPhone and iPad, working with VoiceOver, Spoken Content and anything using the system voices, all on the device and offline.

This build includes voice data that is not part of the open code and belongs to its owners: Centigram Communications, whose TruVoice later passed to Lernout & Hauspie, ScanSoft and Nuance. It is included for personal accessibility use, is not covered by the code licence, and will be removed if a rights holder asks.

versions.localizedDescription:
# iTruVoice 1.0.7

Two sideload variants of the same build — pick the rate you prefer:

- **16k (hifi)**: OpenTV's own third sample rate. Genuinely more
  bandwidth than the classic rate, same voices. Try this one first.
- **11k (classic)**: the original TruVoice desktop rate.

New since 1.0.6: the Spanish pitch fix (uniform intonation across
voices, lower floor) from upstream, plus everything in 1.0.6: 20
voices (10 English + 10 Spanish under es-ES), engine-level phoneme
fixes for app and brand names, and the text-layer dictionary.

Unsigned: import with SideStore and sign with your own certificate.

# iTruVoice 1.0.6

Two sideload variants of the same build — pick the rate you prefer:

- **16k (hifi)**: OpenTV's own third sample rate. Genuinely more
  bandwidth than the classic rate, same voices. Try this one first.
- **11k (classic)**: the original TruVoice desktop rate.

Both include 20 voices (10 English + 10 Spanish, the Spanish under
es-ES), the engine-level phoneme fixes for app and brand names
(Gmail, Dyson, WhatsApp, GitHub, and 14 more), and the text-layer
dictionary (SideStore, ChatGPT, 300+ more).

Unsigned: import with SideStore and sign with your own certificate.

# iTruVoice 1.0.5

Three engine-layer fixes, all measured against the built engine.

**Your name, said right.** The engine stressed the second syllable
("dev-IN") while Kevin takes the first. The user lexicon now pins Devin to
Kevin-with-a-D, one entry covering every casing, and the possessive comes
along ("Devin's" reads with the same stress). The old Linux entry is gone:
title-case already read exactly as lowercase, and all-caps spell-out happens
before the lexicon can ever see the word.

**"VoiceOver", said as two words.** The compound read as voice plus "eover".
It now speaks with exactly the phonemes two-word "voice over" does, verified
byte-identical on every casing.

**Twice as loud.** The engine peaks at 30–74% of full scale across the ten
voices, so full volume sat below Alex and Keynote Gold. A base lift doubles
every path — VoiceOver and preview alike — with VoiceOver's own volume still
scaling above it, and volume 0 still silencing.

Verified by the host corpus check and the CoreChecks suite, which now pins
the boost and its clamping.
